1.text: Pleased. Wisdom still speaks. Solomon often makes similar division, to make the deeper impression. Prov. xxx. 15. 24.

4.text: Fool. Gr. "adulterer, devoid of sense." Is. lxv. 20. C. --- Luxuria...senectuti fœdissima. Cic. off. i.

5.text: Age? Wisdom, says Bias, "is more durable than other possessions." Laert.

9.text: Things. Gr. "nine suppositions I have blessed in my heart," (H.) or thought that they may confer felicity. But the tenth will certainly do it. C. xiv.

10.text: Enemies. Not out of revenge, but for the glory of God. See Matt. v. 43.

14.text: Things. Gr. adds, "for light (15.) he that," &c. H.

16.text: It. This is not in the edit. of Rome, or of Aldus: but it is in the rest. Fear commonly begins the work of salvation, and love perfects it. 1 Tim. i. 5. C. --- All happiness in this life is grounded on the fear of God. W.

17.text: Evil. Gr. reads not this; but the Syriac does, omitting the two next verses. C. --- Heresy is described under the idea of a wicked woman, concealing her malice. W.

18.text: Choose. Lit. "see." H. --- Some supply "send any plague," &c.

21.text: Enemies. Which they wish, or may behold. C. xviii. 31. C.

22.text: Head. Or poison, as the Heb. rosh signifies both. Rondet.

23.text: Woman. Gr. "enemy." C. --- Revenge is the passion of little souls, and of women. Juv. xiii. --- Dragon. This is not exaggerated, if we reflect on the evils occasioned by Eve, Dalila, Athalia, &c. C. --- "A woman is the greatest wild-beast." Menander.

24.text: Sackcloth. And is black when passion bursts forth, though women too frequently conceal their anger to take deeper vengeance.

25.text: Groaned. Gr. "shall fall." --- Little. Gr. "bitterly." He cannot avoid hearing of his wife's misconduct. H. --- She will raise him enemies on all sides.

26.text: Her. I could wish no greater evil to the worst of enemies. Eccles. vii. 27.

27.text: Man. He cannot advance. C. --- Semper habet lites. Juv. vi.

28.text: Beauty. Other qualifications of more importance must be regarded. H. --- He should choose one who may be a companion and assistant in domestic concerns. Grot.

30.text: A. Gr. "If she bring a fortune to her husband," (H.) she will continually upbraid him with it, and cover him with confusion. v. 29. C. --- Lay-leadership in spiritual things is so unreasonable, that few heretics will endure it. W.

32.text: Happy. A lazy wife will give no content.

33.text: Die. Eve tempted her husband, and thus we are all involved in sin. 1 Tim. ii. 14.

34.text: Water. Incontinency. C. xxvi. 15. Prov. v. 15. If water find a hole, it will presently flow away. Women were kept much at home in the East, as they are in many parts of Europe. C. --- Retirement and silence are the characteristics of a wise woman. Æschyl. Thebas.

35.text: She will. Gr. "cut her off from thy flesh." Grabe and Comp. add, (H.) "give a bill of divorce or her dowry, and send her away." C.
